evidence.observation: Plan: "U2–U6 and U8 skip every element whose origin is an include; those elements were validated standalone at resolution step 8 under their own file's rules". The section 6 control is "the attribution lines of VG3 name every include and its confirmed count on each validate". In src/gnd/model/_includes.py the standalone check keeps only `severity == 'error'` issues. D-03 (_validation.py:1409-1450, `semantic:modality-policy`) is only a warning for a proposed llm-inferred/common-sense/induced alethic constraint, and outside the unattended mode nothing refuses `explicit`/`user-supplied` without a reviewer. So a file the unattended host writes itself, with no mode, can carry proposed llm-inferred alethic constraints or explicit-sourced claims. Included, those bypass U3 and U8 under the root, and the attribution line counts only `confirmed`, so they are not even counted.

concerns.recommendation: Narrow the exemption: keep U8 (and the D-03 condition) for included constraints that are not `confirmed`, or require each included file to declare a non-`none` reviewer. Widen the D5 attribution to count alethic and unconfirmed-alethic constraints and non-proposed sources. Add a VG3 criterion where an included file with a proposed llm-inferred alethic constraint is refused, or at least flagged, under an unattended root. Section 6 should state the residual trust assumption as a named limit, not as a control.
concerns.title: Include exemption lets an unattended root carry unreviewed alethic or explicit claims as if reviewed

evidence.observation: R0.4 says root-owned elements are "checked by U1–U8 exactly as today", and section 6 claims "VG3-C2 and VG3-C3, one case per rule and one for an attached constraint". But VG3-C2 tests only "exit 3 with U2, U3, U4" and VG3-C3 only "U5". No case covers U6 (root-owned sample rows without sample_spans), U7 (a root-owned span naming an undeclared document) or U8 (a root-owned alethic sample/llm-inferred constraint). In _merge (_includes.py:162-167), a root constraint attached to an included fact type lands at `$.fact_types[k].constraints[n]` with origin 'model', inside a fact type whose origin is `includes[ID]`. An origin skip keyed on the fact type rather than the constraint would silently exempt it from U8.

concerns.recommendation: Extend VG3-C2/C3 to one root-owned case each for U6, U7 and U8, including a U8 case on an alethic `sample` constraint attached to an included fact type, so the shared origin test is pinned at constraint granularity.
concerns.title: R0.4 claims every U rule is kept, but the criteria test only U2–U5

evidence.location: VG3 goal; section 2 VG3; section 10 open questions
evidence.observation: The goal and section 2 exempt included elements from "U2–U6 and U8", which implies U7 still applies to them, yet the open questions defer "what U7 does with a span an included element carries". In _unattended.py:207-226, U7 is emitted only as span_rule_id inside the U4/U5/U6 walks, so skipping included elements in those walks also drops U7 for them. The plan's rule text and the code's structure point different ways. A reviewed seed's spans name documents the root does not declare, so applying U7 would refuse the #222 root that VG3-C1 requires to pass.

concerns.recommendation: Decide in the plan, not the spec, that U7 is exempt for included elements (consistent with VG3-C1 and VG3-C5), list it in the D3 exemption, and test it.
concerns.title: Whether U7 applies to included elements is unresolved and conflicts with VG3-C1

evidence.location: section 5 Compatibility; section 2 VG3 span walk; VG3-C5
evidence.observation: Plan: "VG2 (a) and VG3 (a) admit inputs that 0.4.0 refuses and refuse nothing 0.4.0 admits" and "0.4.0 admits no unattended include root at all (H14), so no shipped model is affected". Today _includes.py refuses only an included file whose own mode is unattended, and _rule_unattended runs over the merged document. So an unattended root whose included elements are proposed, not explicit, and carry spans citing a root-declared document validates in 0.4.0. H25's workaround, with the seed file as the root's first document, is that shape. For such roots, VG3-C5 ("span counts cover root-owned spans only") stops re-hashing the included spans that 0.4.0 checks, which changes `--require-documents` output and weakens integrity. D6 also refuses a repin-include that 0.4.0 admits on them.

concerns.recommendation: Correct the compatibility statement. Either keep re-hashing an included element's span when it names a document the root declares, or state the behaviour change, and add a criterion pinning a 0.4.0-valid unattended include root's validate output.
concerns.title: The claim that 0.4.0 admits no unattended include root is false, so VG3 changes output for valid roots

evidence.observation: VG3-C8: "an issue on an included object type carries `includes[ID]:` (H17)". H17's only producer is U4 on included object types, which VG3 exempts. After VG3, no CLI path is left that produces the issue the criterion tests. If remap_issues is widened for every root, VG3-C7's "byte-identical `gnd validate` output" for non-unattended include roots also needs a check.

concerns.recommendation: Name the producer in the plan, or restate VG3-C8 as a unit test of remap_issues over a synthetic `$.object_types[id=…]` issue plus a VG3-C7 case on a non-unattended include root.

response.summary: The plan's code and document citations match the checkout (universe.py:59/218/299/358, semantic_adapter.py:610-611/707, _includes.py:222-237 and remap_issues, _enforce_d12 at service.py:402-477, evolution contract lines 258/279-280/618-664, representation-format.md:1845-1847/1905-1915, pyproject.toml:79). The risk table says, "An unattended host writes its own \"reviewed\" include and so carries `confirmed` claims into an unattended model" and "GND cannot know who wrote a file". evidence.observation: D4 admits no documents "while the root owns no object type, fact type or constraint", but the risk control claims "U1 stays whenever the root owns an element". Operations and their obligations are root-owned provenance-bearing claims; current U2 examines them, while U4, U5 and the span walk do not require their spans. evidence.observation: VG3 promises, "Every included element is reported with its include." D5 instead specifies "one line per include" containing counts, and VG3-C6 checks only those lines. concerns.title: VG3’s reporting criterion does not demonstrate its per-element claim

evidence.observation: VG1-C2–C5 require "under 10 s in process", a wall-time doubling ratio, and "under 20 s" without specifying reference hardware or load. The plan acknowledges a "flaky" time-bound test on a loaded machine. The draft VG1 spec, line 198, uses the minimum of three runs for the ratio, which still depends on runner speed and contention.

concerns.recommendation: Specify a reproducible performance environment for the absolute bounds and make a machine-independent work or call-count invariant the required regression gate.
concerns.title: VG1 acceptance depends on the machine running the tests

criteria: MVP first: classify every concern as blocking, hardening, or completeness, and report blocking concerns first. A concern is blocking only if, left unfixed, the software does not demonstrably do what it claims. Do not manufacture completeness concerns to avoid an empty return -- "no concerns, and here is what I checked" is a valid answer.
For this plan, a concern is blocking only if, left unfixed, a phase cannot be specified, implemented or tested as written, or the milestone would not do what its goal claims.

Can each phase VG1, VG2, VG3, VG4 and VG5 be specified, implemented and tested as section 2 and section 4 write it, within the scope sections 1 and 7 state? Is any criterion in section 4 impossible, unfalsifiable or dependent on one machine's speed?
